title: Retail Installment Contracts and Repossession and Collateral Recovery: Recovery Review Charge on Hardship Extensions
content:
A hardship extension on a contract under Retail Installment Contracts carries a recovery review charge read from the contract's repossession cases under Repossession and Collateral Recovery — how each case closed, the case's closing date and, for a recalled case, its recall reason.

**Rule.**

1. When the contract's repossession case closed as **reinstated** (a contract is reinstated at most once) and its closing date is later than the same calendar day **24** months before the effective date (the last day of that month when that day does not exist), the fee adds **15.00**.
2. When that is not so, but a repossession case on the contract closed as **recalled** with the recall reason *account brought current*, the fee adds **10.00**.
3. Otherwise it adds nothing.

| Repossession case history | Recovery review charge |
|---|---|
| reinstated case closed within the 24 months | 15.00 |
| reinstated case closed on or before the 24-month mark, plus a case recalled as account brought current | 10.00 |
| no reinstated case, a case recalled as account brought current | 10.00 |
| reinstated case closed on or before the 24-month mark, nothing else | nothing |
| a case recalled for any other reason, or no case | nothing |

**Boundary (hypothetical, effective date 9 March).** A reinstated case closed 10 March two years earlier is inside the window (15.00); one closed 9 March two years earlier is not later than the mark and falls to rule 2 or 3.
